sentences.zh: 梁祖之開國也，屬黃巢大亂之後。

translations.literal: When the founder of Liang established his state, it was after the great disorder of Huang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Liang founder founded his dynasty, the realm was still reeling from Huang Chao's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 以夷門一鎮，外嚴烽侯，內辟汙萊，厲以耕桑，薄以租賦，士雖苦戰，民則樂輸，二紀之間，俄成霸業。

translations.literal: With one commandery at Yimen, outwardly he tightened beacon and frontier defense, inwardly he opened up waste and marshland, urged farming and sericulture, kept rent and tax light; though soldiers suffered in battle, the people were glad to pay in, and within two reign-periods he soon achieved hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: From a single stronghold at Yimen he tightened frontier defenses abroad and reclaimed wasteland at home, promoted farming and silk production, and kept taxes low. Soldiers bore the hardships of war, yet commoners paid levies willingly; within roughly twenty years he had built a hegemonic power.

sentences.zh: 及末帝與莊宗對壘於河上，河南之民，雖困於輦運，亦未至流亡，其義無他，蓋賦斂輕而丘園可戀故也。

translations.literal: When the last emperor and Zhuangzong faced each other across the Yellow River, the people of Henan, though strained by cart transport levies, still did not reach the point of flight; the reason was none other than that collections were light and homesteads worth holding.
translations.idiomatic: When the last Liang emperor and Li Cunxu faced off along the Yellow River, Henan commoners were worn down by supply transport but did not yet flee en masse—because levies remained tolerable and families still had reason to cling to their farms.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗平定梁室，任吏人孔謙為租庸使，峻法以剝下，厚斂以奉上，民產雖竭，軍食尚虧。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified the Liang house, he appointed the clerk Kong Qian as transport-and-corvée commissioner, using harsh laws to strip the lower ranks and heavy collection to supply the court; though popular wealth was exhausted, army provisions were still short.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong overthrew the Liang, he put the clerk Kong Qian in charge of transport and corvée taxes, enforcing harsh exactions on the populace while heaping revenue on the court. Private wealth was drained dry, yet military rations still fell short.

sentences.zh: 加之以兵革，因之以饑饉，不三四年，以致顛隕，其義無他，蓋賦役重而寰區失望故也。

translations.literal: Added to this were weapons and armor, followed by famine; in less than three or four years he came to ruin—the reason, again, was none other than that levies and labor service were heavy and the realm lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: War piled on top of famine, and within three or four years the Tang founder's regime collapsed—for no other reason than crushing taxes and corvée that left the empire disillusioned.

sentences.zh: （案：以上見《容齋三筆》所引《薛史》，繹其文義，當系《食貨志序》，今錄於卷首。）〉

translations.idiomatic: (Editorial note: The passage above appears in Hong Mai's Third Brush Notes as a quotation from the Old History; by its sense it belongs to the preface of this Finance treatise and is placed here at the chapter opening.)]

sentences.zh: 唐同光三年二月，敕：「魏府小菉豆稅，每畝減放三升。

translations.literal: Tang, second month of Tongguang year 3, edict: 'The small green-bean tax of Weifu is reduced by three sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tongguang 3 (925), an edict ordered: "Reduce the Weifu green-bean levy by three sheng per mu.

sentences.zh: 城內店宅園囿，比來無稅，頃因偽命，遂有配征。

translations.literal: Shops, residences, and gardens within the city had until now been untaxed; recently, because of a false order, there came assigned collection.
translations.idiomatic: Shops, houses, and gardens inside the city had long been untaxed, but a spurious order had recently imposed assessments on them.

sentences.zh: 後來以所征物色，添助軍裝衣賜，將令通濟，宜示矜蠲。

translations.literal: Later the goods collected were added to aid military kit and clothing grants, intending to make things flow; compassion and remission should be shown.
translations.idiomatic: The proceeds had been earmarked to supplement army uniforms and grants, but to keep commerce viable the levy should be lifted as a gesture of relief.

sentences.zh: 今據緊慢去處，於見輸稅絲上，每兩作三等，酌量納錢，收市軍裝衣賜，其絲仍與除放。

translations.literal: Now according to whether places are tight or slack, on silk already paid in tax, each liang is divided into three grades, with measured cash payment to purchase military kit and clothing grants; the silk itself is still to be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, depending on local conditions, each liang of silk already due in tax shall be split into three grades and commuted to cash at assessed rates to fund uniforms and grants, while the silk obligation itself is waived.

sentences.zh: 」其年閏十二月，吏部尚書李琪上言：「請賦稅不以折納為事，一切以本色輸官，又不以紐配為名，止以正稅加納。

translations.literal: ' That year, intercalary twelfth month, Minister of Personnel Li Qi submitted: 'I ask that land tax not take conversion payment as its business, that everything be delivered to the government in kind, and that there be no extra collection under the name of paired allotment—only the regular tax with added payment.'
translations.idiomatic: " In the intercalary twelfth month of that year, Li Qi, Minister of Personnel, memorialized: "Stop using commutation for tax payments; deliver all dues in kind to the government, and abolish surcharges disguised as paired allotments—charge only the standard tax."

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「本朝征科，惟配有兩稅，至於折納，當不施為。

translations.literal: ' Edict: 'This dynasty's collections allow only paired allotment with the two taxes; as for conversion payment, it should not be applied.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne replied: "Our collections permit only the paired allotments tied to the two-tax system; commutation must not be used.

sentences.zh: 宜依李琪所論，應逐稅合納錢物斛斗鹽錢等，宜令租庸司指揮，並準元征本色輸納，不得改更，若合有移改，即須具事由聞奏。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to follow Li Qi's argument: all items due in tax—cash, goods, bushels, pecks, salt money, and the like—should be directed by the Transport and Corvée Office to be paid in the original levied kind, without alteration; if change is appropriate, the reasons must be reported in a memorial.'
translations.idiomatic: Follow Li Qi's proposal: the Transport and Corvée Office shall order that every tax item—cash, grain, salt dues, and the rest—be paid in the originally assessed kind without substitution; any change requires a memorial stating the reasons."

sentences.zh: 長興二年六月，敕：「委諸道觀察使，屬縣於每村定有力人戶充村長。

translations.literal: Changxing year 2, sixth month, edict: 'Commission the circuit observation commissioners: in subordinate counties, in each village fix a strong household to serve as village head.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Changxing 2 (931), an edict directed circuit commissioners to appoint a leading household in each village as village head.

sentences.zh: 與村人議，有力人戶出剩田苗，補貧下不迨，肯者即具狀征收，有辭者即排段檢括。

translations.literal: Deliberate with villagers: strong households contribute surplus field seedlings to supplement the poor who cannot keep up; those willing submit a written statement for collection, those who refuse undergo parcel-by-parcel inspection and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: They were to consult villagers so wealthy households could contribute surplus harvest assessments to cover shortfalls among the poor; volunteers would register for collection, while holdouts would be surveyed parcel by parcel.

sentences.zh: 自今年起為定額。

translations.literal: From this year onward it becomes a fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: From that year forward the arrangement became a fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 有經災沴及逐年逋處，不在此限。

translations.literal: Places that have suffered disaster or yearly arrears are outside this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Areas hit by disaster or chronic arrears were exempt.

sentences.zh: 」三年十二月，三司奏請：「諸道上供稅物，充兵士衣賜不足。

translations.literal: ' Twelfth month, year 3, the Three Departments memorialized: 'The tax goods presented by the circuits are insufficient to cover soldiers' clothing grants.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth month of year 3, the Three Departments reported that circuit tribute was insufficient for soldiers' clothing grants.

sentences.zh: 其天下所納斛斗及錢，除支贍外，請依時折納綾羅絹帛。

translations.literal: Of grain and cash submitted from the realm, after disbursement for upkeep, we ask that according to the season they be converted to silk, gauze, and cloth.'
translations.idiomatic: They requested that grain and cash collected empire-wide, after meeting current expenses, be commuted seasonally into silks and textiles.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ' Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 晉天福四年正月，敕：「應諸道節度刺史，不得擅加賦役及於縣邑別立監征。

translations.literal: Jin, first month of Tianfu year 4, edict: 'All circuit military commissioners and prefects must not on their own add levies and labor service, nor separately establish supervisory collection in counties and towns.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jin Tianfu 4 (939), an edict forbade military commissioners and prefects from imposing extra levies or setting up separate collection offices in counties.

sentences.zh: 所納田租，委人戶自量自既。」

translations.literal: Field rent paid in is entrusted to households to measure and deliver themselves.'
translations.idiomatic: Field rent was to be measured and delivered by the paying households themselves."

sentences.zh: 周顯德三年十月，宣三司指揮諸道州府，今後夏稅，以六月一日起征，秋稅至十月一日起征，永為定制。

translations.literal: Zhou, tenth month of Xiande year 3: the Three Departments proclaimed to all circuit prefectures and districts that henceforth summer tax collection begins on the first day of the sixth month and autumn tax on the first day of the tenth month, permanently as fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Zhou Xiande 3 (956), the Three Departments ordered all circuits that summer tax would be collected from the first day of the sixth month and autumn tax from the first day of the tenth month, permanently.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，賜諸道《均田圖》。

translations.literal: Seventh month, year 5, the Diagram of Equalized Fields was bestowed on the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 5, each circuit received a copy of the Equal-Field Diagram.

sentences.zh: 十月，命左散騎常侍艾穎等三十四人，下諸州檢定民租。

translations.literal: Tenth month: Left Regular Attendant Ai Ying and thirty-four others were ordered down to the prefectures to examine and fix popular rent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, thirty-four officials led by Ai Ying, Left Regular Attendant, were sent to the prefectures to audit household rents.

sentences.zh: 周顯德六年春，諸道使臣回，總計檢到戶二百三十萬九千八百一十二。

translations.literal: Zhou, spring of Xiande year 6: when the circuit envoys returned, the total households examined came to 2,309,812.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xiande 6 (959), after envoys returned from the circuits, the audit registered 2,309,812 households.

sentences.zh: 唐同光二年，度支奏請榜示府州縣鎮，軍民商旅凡有買賣，並須使八十陌錢。

translations.literal: Tang, Tongguang year 2: the Revenue Office memorialized requesting placards in prefectures, districts, counties, and market towns that all military and civilian travelers in commerce must use 'eighty per hundred' cash.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 2 (924), the Revenue Office ordered placards in every administrative seat requiring all buyers and sellers, military or civilian, to use cash counted at eighty per hundred full value.

sentences.zh: 唐同光二年二月，詔曰：「錢者，古之泉布，蓋取其流行天下，布散人間，無積滯則交易通，多貯藏則士農困，故西漢興改幣之制，立告緡之條，所以權蓄賈而防大奸也。

translations.literal: Tang, Tongguang year 2, second month, edict: 'Cash is the ancient spring and cloth currency—so called because it circulates under Heaven and spreads among men. Without hoarding, trade flows; with much storing, scholar and farmer suffer. Thus the Western Han, when it rose, changed coinage and established the report-hoarding statute, thereby balancing stored wealth and preventing great villainy.
translations.idiomatic: A Tongguang 2 edict explained: "Coin is the ancient currency called 'spring and cloth' because it should circulate widely. When it does not stagnate, trade thrives; when the wealthy hoard it, farmers and gentry suffer. That is why the Western Han reformed coinage and required reporting of hoards—to curb merchants' stockpiling and major fraud."

sentences.zh: 宜令所司散下州府，常須檢察，不得令富室分外收貯見錢，又工人銷鑄為銅器，兼沿邊州鎮設法鈐轄，勿令商人般載出境。

translations.literal: Let the responsible offices send this down to prefectures and districts; they must constantly inspect, not allow wealthy houses to take in and store extra ready cash, nor workers to melt and cast it into copper vessels; along the frontier prefectures and posts methods of control are also to be set so merchants do not transport it out of the border.'
translations.idiomatic: Responsible offices were to circulate the order to all prefectures, forbid wealthy households from hoarding cash, stop artisans from melting coin into copperware, and tighten frontier controls so merchants could not export currency.

sentences.zh: 」三月，知唐州晏駢安奏：「市肆間點檢錢帛，內有錫镴小錢，揀得不少，皆是江南綱商挾帶而來。

translations.literal: ' Third month: Yan Pian'an, Tangzhou prefect, memorialized: 'In markets, when cash and cloth are inspected, among them are tin-lead small coins; quite a number were picked out, all brought along by Jiangnan convoy merchants.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third month, Yan Pian'an, prefect of Tangzhou, reported that market inspections of currency had turned up many tin-lead small coins, all smuggled in by Jiangnan merchant convoys.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「帛布之幣，雜以鉛錫，惟是江湖之外，盜鑄尤多，市肆之間，公行無畏，因是綱商挾帶，舟楫往來，換易好錢，藏貯富室，實為蠹弊，須有條流。

translations.literal: ' Edict: 'Cloth currency adulterated with lead and tin—only beyond the rivers and lakes is illicit casting especially great; in markets it is done openly without fear. Hence convoy merchants carry it, boats come and go, exchanging for good cash and storing it in wealthy houses—truly a borer's harm; regulations are needed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court replied that debased cloth coin mixed with lead and tin flourished chiefly south of the Yangtze, where counterfeiters operated openly in markets. Convoys shuttled the bad money in, traded it for good coin, and wealthy houses hoarded it—a serious abuse requiring new rules.

sentences.zh: 宜令京城、諸道，於坊市行使錢內，點檢雜惡鉛錫錢，並宜禁斷。

translations.literal: Let the capital and all circuits, in cash circulating in wards and markets, inspect and cut off miscellaneous wicked lead-tin cash.'
translations.idiomatic: The capital and every circuit were to inspect currency in urban markets and ban all adulterated lead-tin coin.

sentences.zh: 沿江州縣，每有舟船到岸，嚴加覺察，不許將雜鉛錫惡錢往來換易好錢，如有私載，並行收納。」

translations.literal: Along-river prefectures and districts: whenever boats reach shore, observe strictly; do not allow miscellaneous lead-tin wicked cash to come and go exchanging for good cash—if privately carried, all is to be confiscated.'
translations.idiomatic: Riverine prefectures were to scrutinize every arriving vessel and forbid exchanging debased coin for good money; any private shipment was to be confiscated.

sentences.zh: 天成元年八月，中書門下奏：「訪聞近日諸道州府所賣銅器價貴，多是銷熔見錢，以邀厚利。

translations.literal: Tiancheng year 1, eighth month: the Secretariat memorialized: 'We have learned that recently in circuit prefectures and districts, copper vessels sold are costly—mostly from melting ready cash to seek thick profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tiancheng 1 (926), the Secretariat reported that copperware prices had risen across the circuits because artisans were melting circulating cash for profit.

sentences.zh: 」乃下詔曰：「宜令遍行曉告，如元舊系銅器及碎銅，即許鑄造器物。

translations.literal: ' Then an edict: 'It is fitting to proclaim everywhere: if originally registered copper vessels and scrap copper, casting vessels is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed ordering public notice that only registered old copperware and scrap copper might be cast into new vessels.

sentences.zh: 仍生銅器物每斤價定二百文，熟銅器物每斤四百文，如違省價，買賣之人依盜鑄錢律文科斷。」

translations.literal: Raw-copper vessels are fixed at two hundred cash per jin, wrought-copper vessels at four hundred cash per jin; if prices are cut below this, buyers and sellers are sentenced under the statute on illicit coin casting.'
translations.idiomatic: Raw copperware was capped at two hundred cash per jin and wrought copperware at four hundred; anyone selling below those prices would be punished under the illicit-coining statute."

sentences.zh: 清泰二年十二月，詔御史臺曉告中外，禁用鉛錢，如違犯，準條流處分。

translations.literal: Qingtai year 2, twelfth month: edict that the Censorate proclaim inside and outside, forbidding lead cash; violators are handled according to the code.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Qingtai 2 (935), the Censorate was ordered to announce empire-wide prohibition of lead coin, with violations punished under statute.

sentences.zh: 晉天福二年，詔：「禁一切銅器，其銅鏡今後官鑄造，於東京置場貨賣，許人收買，於諸處興販去。」

translations.literal: Jin, Tianfu year 2, edict: 'Forbid all copper vessels; copper mirrors hereafter are to be cast by the government, with a market set up at the Eastern Capital for sale, allowing people to buy and trade them elsewhere.'
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Tianfu 2 (937), all private copperware was banned; mirrors would be minted by the state and sold at an Eastern Capital depot for resale elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 周廣順元年三月，敕：「銅法，今後官中更不禁斷，一任興販，所在一色即不得瀉破為銅器貨賣，如有犯者，有人糾告捉獲，所犯人不計多少斤兩，並處死。

translations.literal: Zhou, Guangshun year 1, third month, edict: 'On copper law: hereafter the court no longer forbids it; trade is entirely free—but locally, cash must not be melted and broken into copper vessels for sale. If there are violators and someone reports and seizes them, the offender, regardless of how many jin, is all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Guangshun 1 (951), copper trade was legalized, but melting coin into copperware for sale remained a capital crime on report and arrest, regardless of quantity.

sentences.zh: 其地分所由節級，決脊杖十七放，鄰保人決臀杖十七放，其告事人給與賞錢一百貫文。」

translations.literal: The local officer and rank in charge receive seventeen strokes of the cudgel on the back and release; neighbor-guarantors receive seventeen strokes on the buttocks and release; the informant is given a reward of one hundred strings of cash.'
translations.idiomatic: Local officers received seventeen strokes on the back, neighbor guarantors seventeen on the buttocks, and informants a reward of one hundred strings of cash."

sentences.zh: 江南因唐舊制，饒州置永平監，歲鑄錢，池州永寧監、建州永豐監，並歲鑄錢，杭州置保興監鑄錢。

translations.literal: Jiangnan, following Tang's old system, set Yongping Mint at Raozhou casting cash yearly; Yongning Mint at Chizhou and Yongfeng Mint at Jianzhou also cast yearly; Hangzhou set Baoxing Mint to cast cash.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan followed Tang precedent: Raozhou's Yongping mint, Chizhou's Yongning mint, and Jianzhou's Yongfeng mint coined annually, while Hangzhou's Baoxing mint was also established.

sentences.zh: 唐同光二年二月，詔曰：「會計之重，鹹鹺居先，矧彼兩池，實有豐利。

translations.literal: Tang, Tongguang year 2, second month, edict: 'In the weight of accounts, salt comes first—how much more those two pools, which truly have abundant profit.
translations.idiomatic: A Tongguang 2 edict declared that in state finance salt revenue ranked first—and the two salt pools were especially lucrative.

sentences.zh: 頃自兵戈擾攘，民庶流離，既場務以隳殘，致程課之虧失。

translations.literal: Recently, since weapons and armor disturbed the realm, the people drifted away; the field offices were ruined, causing scheduled levies to fall short.
translations.idiomatic: War had scattered the population and wrecked the salt offices, so scheduled revenues had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 重茲葺理，須仗規模，將立事以成功，在從長而就便。

translations.literal: To restore this again, regulations must be relied on; to establish affairs and achieve success lies in following what is longer and taking what is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Restoration required firm regulations and pragmatic policies that could actually succeed.

sentences.zh: 宜令河中節度使冀王李繼麟兼充制置度支安邑、解縣兩池榷鹽使，便可制，一一條貫。」

translations.literal: Let Hedong military commissioner Prince of Ji Li Jilin also serve as commissioner for planning revenue and monopoly salt commissioner of the two pools at Anyi and Jie counties; he may at once draw up regulations, item by item.'
translations.idiomatic: Prince Li Jilin of Ji, military commissioner of Hedong, was appointed monopoly salt commissioner for the Anyi and Jie pools and authorized to draft comprehensive regulations immediately."

translations.literal: open editorial bracket

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》：同光三年二月，敕：「魏府每年所征隨絲鹽錢，每兩與減放五文；

translations.literal: (Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium: Tongguang year 3, second month, edict: 'Weifu's yearly salt money levied with silk tax is reduced five cash per liang;
translations.idiomatic: (From the Five Dynasties Institutional Compendium: In Tongguang 3, an edict reduced Weifu's silk-linked salt surcharge by five cash per liang;

sentences.zh: 逐年亻表賣蠶鹽、食鹽、大鹽、甜次冷鹽，每鬥與減五十；

translations.literal: each year allotted sale of silkworm salt, table salt, coarse salt, and sweet secondary cold salt—each dou is reduced by fifty;
translations.idiomatic: annual allotments of silkworm salt, table salt, coarse salt, and secondary cold salt were cut by fifty cash per dou;

sentences.zh: 欒鹽與減三十。

translations.literal: Luan salt is reduced by thirty.
translations.idiomatic: and Luan salt by thirty.

sentences.zh: 」天成元年四月，敕：「諸州府百姓合散蠶鹽，今後每年只二月內一度亻表散，依夏稅限納錢。

translations.literal: ' Tiancheng year 1, fourth month, edict: 'Silkworm salt that prefectures and districts should distribute to commoners—hereafter each year only once within the second month is it allotted; payment follows the summer-tax deadline.
translations.idiomatic: " In Tiancheng 1, silkworm-salt distribution to households was limited to a single allotment each February, with payment due on the summer-tax schedule.

sentences.zh: 」長興四年五月七日，諸道鹽錢轉運使奏：「諸道州府鹽法條流元末，一概定奪，謹具如後：應食顆鹽州府，省司各置榷糶折博場院。

translations.literal: ' Changxing year 4, fifth month, seventh day: the circuit salt-and-cash transport commissioner memorialized: 'Salt-law provisions in circuit prefectures and districts originally had no end; we have settled them uniformly and respectfully list them below: In prefectures with granular edible salt, each provincial office sets monopoly sale and barter yards.
translations.idiomatic: " On the seventh day of the fifth month of Changxing 4, the salt transport commissioner submitted unified salt regulations: prefectures selling granular salt were to maintain state monopoly and barter depots.

sentences.zh: 應是鄉村，並通私商興販。

translations.literal: All villages may freely allow private merchants to trade.
translations.idiomatic: Villages might still permit private trade.

sentences.zh: 所有折博並每年人戶蠶鹽，並不許將帶一斤一兩入城，侵奪榷糶課利。

translations.literal: All barter goods and yearly household silkworm salt are not permitted to be brought into cities, even one jin or one liang, encroaching on monopoly-sale revenue.
translations.idiomatic: But barter salt and allotted silkworm salt could not be carried into cities even by the ounce, lest they undercut monopoly profits.

sentences.zh: 如違犯者，一兩已上至一斤，買賣人各杖六十；

translations.literal: Violators: from one liang up to one jin, buyers and sellers each receive sixty blows;
translations.idiomatic: Violators from one liang up to one jin: sixty strokes for buyer and seller alike;

sentences.zh: 一斤已上至三斤，買賣人各杖七十；

translations.literal: from one jin up to three jin, each seventy blows;
translations.idiomatic: from one to three jin: seventy strokes each;

sentences.zh: 三斤已上至五斤，買賣人各杖八十；

translations.literal: from three jin up to five jin, each eighty blows;
translations.idiomatic: from three to five jin: eighty strokes each;

sentences.zh: 五斤已上至十斤，買賣人各徒二年；

translations.literal: from five jin up to ten jin, each penal servitude two years;
translations.idiomatic: from five to ten jin: two years' penal servitude for both parties;

sentences.zh: 十斤已上，不計多少，買賣人各決脊杖二十，處死。

translations.literal: ten jin and above, regardless of amount, buyers and sellers each receive twenty cudgel strokes on the back and execution.
translations.idiomatic: ten jin or more: twenty strokes on the back and execution for buyer and seller, whatever the exact weight.

sentences.zh: 所有犯鹽人隨行錢物、驢畜等，並納入官。

translations.literal: All cash, goods, donkeys, and livestock accompanying salt offenders are confiscated to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Cash, goods, and pack animals accompanying offenders were forfeited to the state.

sentences.zh: 所有元本家業莊田，如是全家逃走者，即行點納。

translations.literal: Original family estates and fields—if the whole family flees, they are immediately assessed and collected.
translations.idiomatic: If an entire family fled, their original farms were assessed and seized.

sentences.zh: 仍許般載腳戶、經過店主並腳下人力等糾告，等第支與優給。

translations.literal: Carriers, passing innkeepers, and porters may report; graded rewards are paid generously.
translations.idiomatic: Carriers, innkeepers, and porters who informed received graded rewards.

sentences.zh: 如知情不告，與賣鹽人同罪。

translations.literal: Those who know but do not report share the salt-seller's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing accomplices who failed to report shared the seller's punishment.

sentences.zh: 其犯鹽人經過處，地分門司、廂界巡檢、節級所由並諸色關連人等，不專覺察，委本州臨時斷訖報省。

translations.literal: Where salt offenders pass, local gate clerks, ward patrol inspectors, rank officers, and all connected persons who do not focus on detection are entrusted to the prefecture for temporary judgment, then reported to the province.
translations.idiomatic: Local gate guards, ward patrols, and officials along the route who failed to detect smuggling were punished by their prefecture and reported upward.

sentences.zh: 如是門司關津口鋪，捉獲私鹽，即依下項等第，支給一半賞錢：十斤以上至五十斤，支賞錢二十千；

translations.literal: If gate offices, passes, or posts seize private salt, rewards follow the grades below, half the bounty paid: ten jin up to fifty jin, twenty thousand cash;
translations.idiomatic: Gate and checkpoint staff who seized illicit salt received half the bounty by grade: twenty thousand cash for ten to fifty jin;

sentences.zh: 五十斤已上至一百斤，支賞錢三十千；

translations.literal: fifty jin up to one hundred jin, thirty thousand cash;
translations.idiomatic: thirty thousand for fifty to one hundred jin;

sentences.zh: 一百斤已上，支賞錢五十千。

translations.literal: one hundred jin and above, fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: fifty thousand for one hundred jin or more.

sentences.zh: 應食末鹽地界，州府縣鎮並有榷糶場院久來內外禁法，即未一概條流。

translations.literal: In territories of powdered edible salt, prefectures, districts, counties, and towns all have monopoly yards with long-standing internal and external prohibitions—not yet unified in provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Powdered-salt regions already had monopoly depots with longstanding prohibitions, not yet codified uniformly.

sentences.zh: 應刮鹹煎鹽，不計多少斤兩，並處極法，兼許四鄰及諸色人等陳告，等第支給賞錢。

translations.literal: Those who scrape brine and boil salt, regardless of weight, all receive the extreme penalty; neighbors and all persons may report, with graded bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Illicit brine boiling, at any quantity, carried the death penalty, with graded rewards for neighbors and others who informed.

sentences.zh: 欲指揮此後犯一兩已上至一斤，買賣人各杖六十；

translations.literal: It is ordered that hereafter, from one liang up to one jin, buyers and sellers each sixty blows;
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, one liang to one jin: sixty strokes each for buyer and seller;

sentences.zh: 一斤已上至二斤，買賣人各杖七十；

translations.literal: one jin up to two jin, each seventy blows;
translations.idiomatic: one to two jin: seventy strokes each;

sentences.zh: 二斤以上至三斤，買賣人各徒一年；

translations.literal: above two jin up to three jin, each one year penal servitude;
translations.idiomatic: two to three jin: one year of penal servitude;

sentences.zh: 三斤以上至五斤，買賣人各徒二年；

translations.literal: above three jin up to five jin, each two years;
translations.idiomatic: three to five jin: two years;

sentences.zh: 五斤已上，買賣人各決脊杖二十，處死。

translations.literal: five jin and above, each twenty back strokes and execution.
translations.idiomatic: five jin or more: twenty strokes on the back and execution.

sentences.zh: 如是收到鹹土鹽水，即委本處煎煉鹽數，準條科斷。

translations.literal: If briny earth or salt water is seized, the local office boils the amount of salt and sentences by statute.
translations.idiomatic: Seized brine or salt soil would be boiled to estimate yield and sentenced accordingly.

sentences.zh: 或有已曾違犯，不至死刑，經斷後公然不懼條流再犯者，不計斤兩多少，所犯人並處極法。

translations.literal: If one has violated before but not reached death, and after judgment openly fears no statute and violates again, regardless of weight, the offender receives the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Repeat offenders who had already been punished but defied the law again faced execution regardless of quantity.

sentences.zh: 其有榷糶場院員僚節級人力、煎鹽池客竈戶、般鹽船綱、押綱軍將衙官梢工等，具知鹽法，如有公然偷盜官鹽，或將貨賣，其買賣人及窩盤主人知情不告，並依前項刮鹹例，五斤已上處死。

translations.literal: Monopoly-yard clerks, rank staff, pool guests, furnace households, salt convoy leaders, escort generals, clerks, and boatmen who fully know salt law—if they openly steal government salt or sell it, buyers and den owners who know and do not report are all under the brine-scraping precedent: five jin and above, execution.
translations.idiomatic: Monopoly clerks, brine workers, convoy guards, and boatmen who stole official salt or sold it, together with knowing buyers and harborers, were sentenced like brine boilers—execution from five jin upward.

sentences.zh: 其諸色關連人等，並合支賞錢，即準洛京邢鎮條流事例指揮。

translations.literal: All connected persons should receive bounty money, following the precedents of Luoyang and Xing prefecture regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Informants among connected parties received rewards according to the Luoyang and Xingzhou precedents.

sentences.zh: 顆、末、青、白等鹽，元不許界分參雜。

translations.literal: Granular, powdered, green, and white salts originally may not be mixed across boundaries.
translations.idiomatic: Granular, powdered, green, and white salts were not to cross regional boundaries.

sentences.zh: 其顆鹽先許通商之時指揮，不得將帶入末鹽地界。

translations.literal: When granular salt was first permitted open trade, the order was that it must not be brought into powdered-salt territory.
translations.idiomatic: When granular salt had been allowed open trade, it still could not enter powdered-salt zones.

sentences.zh: 如有違犯，一斤一兩，並處極法，所有隨行物色，除鹽外，一半納官，一半與捉事人充賞。

translations.literal: If violated, even one jin or one liang receives the extreme penalty; accompanying goods, except salt, half to government, half to captors as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Violations, even of an ounce, brought execution; accompanying property except the salt was split half to the state and half to captors.

sentences.zh: 其餘鹽色，未有畫一條流。

translations.literal: Other salt types have no unified provisions yet.
translations.idiomatic: Other salt types lacked unified rules.

sentences.zh: 其洛京並鎮、定、邢州管內，多北京末鹽入界，捉獲並依洛京條流科斷。

translations.literal: Within Luoyang and Zhen, Ding, and Xing prefectures, much Northern Capital powdered salt enters the border; seizures are sentenced by Luoyang regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang and Zhen, Ding, and Xing prefectures, where northern powdered salt often crossed in, would apply Luoyang penalties on seizure.

sentences.zh: 欲指揮此後但是顆、末、青、白諸色鹽侵界參雜，捉獲並準洛京條流施行。

translations.literal: It is ordered that hereafter any granular, powdered, green, or white salt crossing boundaries is seized and handled by Luoyang regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth any cross-boundary mixing of granular, powdered, green, or white salt would be punished under the Luoyang code.

sentences.zh: 」「一應諸道，今後若捉獲犯私鹽曲人，罪犯分明，正該條法，便仰斷遣訖奏。

translations.literal: ' 'In all circuits, if private-salt offenders are seized and the crime is clear and fits the statute, immediately sentence and memorialize when done.
translations.idiomatic: All circuits: when illicit salt offenders are caught with clear guilt under statute, sentence immediately and memorialize.

sentences.zh: 若稍涉疑誤，只須申奏取裁。」）〉

translations.literal: If there is slight doubt or error, only memorialize for decision.' )〉
translations.idiomatic: If any doubt remains, memorialize for imperial decision.")]

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，河南、河北諸州，除俵散蠶鹽征錢外，每年末鹽界分場務，約糶錢一十七萬貫有餘。

translations.literal: Mid Jin Tianfu, in Henan and Hebei prefectures, besides allotted silkworm-salt levy cash, yearly powdered-salt border offices brought in about more than 170,000 strings from monopoly sale.
translations.idiomatic: During mid-Tianfu, Henan and Hebei monopoly offices for powdered salt, apart from silkworm-salt allotments, yielded over 170,000 strings annually.

sentences.zh: 言事者稱，雖得此錢，百姓多犯鹽法，請將上件食鹽錢於諸道州府計戶，每戶一貫至二百，為五等配之，然後任人逐便興販，既不虧官，又益百姓。

translations.literal: Memorialists said: though this cash is obtained, commoners often violate salt law; they ask to take the above table-salt money, count households in circuit prefectures, assign each household from one string down to two hundred cash in five grades, then let people trade freely—neither harming the state nor failing to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that despite the revenue, salt violations were rampant; they proposed distributing the table-salt levy across households in five grades from one string down to two hundred cash, then allowing free trade—benefiting both state and people.

sentences.zh: 朝廷行之，諸處場務亦且仍舊。

translations.literal: The court carried it out; local offices also remained as before for the time.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted the plan while leaving local offices temporarily unchanged.

sentences.zh: 俄而鹽貨頓賤，去出鹽遠處州縣，每斤不過二十文，近處不過一十文，掌事者又難驟改其法，奏請重制鹽場稅，蓋欲絕其興販，歸利於官也。

translations.literal: Soon salt goods abruptly fell cheap; in distant prefectures and districts from salt sources, each jin was no more than twenty cash, nearby no more than ten. Those in charge found it hard to change the law quickly and memorialized to reimpose salt-yard tax, intending to cut off trade and return profit to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Salt prices soon collapsed—to twenty cash per jin far from production centers and ten nearby. Officials, unable to reverse course quickly, petitioned to restore salt-yard taxes to choke private trade and reclaim revenue.

sentences.zh: 周廣順元年九月，詔改鹽法，凡犯五斤已上者處死，煎鹼鹽犯一斤已上者處死。

translations.literal: Zhou, Guangshun year 1, ninth month: edict revising salt law—violations of five jin and above are executed; boiling alkaline salt, one jin and above is executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Guangshun 1, salt law was revised: smuggling five jin or more merited death, as did boiling alkaline brine from one jin upward.

sentences.zh: 先是漢法不計斤兩多少，並處極刑，至是始革之。

translations.literal: Earlier Han law, regardless of weight, all received the extreme penalty; only now was it first reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Later Han rules had imposed capital punishment regardless of quantity; this was the first reform.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，詔曰：「青白池務，素有定規，只自近年，頗乖循守。

translations.literal: Year 3, third month, edict: 'The green-and-white pool offices have long had fixed rules; only in recent years they have greatly departed from observance.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 3, an edict noted that the green and white salt pools had long had fixed rules but recent years had seen serious departures.

sentences.zh: 比來青鹽一石，抽稅錢八百文足陌、鹽一斗；

translations.literal: Recently on one shi of green salt, tax was drawn of eight hundred cash at full count and one dou of salt;
translations.idiomatic: Recently green salt had been taxed at eight hundred full-value cash plus one dou of salt per shi;

sentences.zh: 白鹽一石，抽稅錢五百文、鹽五升。

translations.literal: on one shi of white salt, five hundred cash and five sheng of salt.
translations.idiomatic: white salt at five hundred cash and five sheng of salt per shi.

sentences.zh: 其後青鹽一石，抽錢一千、鹽一斗。

translations.literal: Afterward on one shi of green salt, one thousand cash and one dou of salt were drawn.
translations.idiomatic: Later the green-salt levy rose to one thousand cash and one dou per shi.

sentences.zh: 訪聞更改已來，不便商販，蕃人漢戶，求利艱難，宜與優饒，庶令存濟。

translations.literal: Upon inquiry it is heard that since the changes, commerce and trade have been inconvenient; Tibetan peoples and Han households find it hard to seek profit; they should be given preferential relief, so that survival may be secured.
translations.idiomatic: Reports indicate that since the rate changes, trade has suffered and both frontier peoples and Han residents struggle to turn a profit; preferential relief is warranted to keep them solvent.

sentences.zh: 今後每青鹽一石，依舊抽稅錢八百文，以八十五為陌，鹽一斗；

translations.literal: Henceforth on each shi of green salt, tax shall be drawn as before at eight hundred cash, with eighty-five as the count per hundred, and one dou of salt;
translations.idiomatic: Going forward, green salt shall again be taxed at eight hundred cash per shi at the eighty-five-count rate, plus one dou of salt;

sentences.zh: 白鹽一石，抽稅錢五百，鹽五升。

translations.literal: On one shi of white salt, five hundred cash in tax is drawn, and five sheng of salt.
translations.idiomatic: White salt shall be taxed at five hundred cash and five sheng per shi.

sentences.zh: 此外更不得別有邀求。

translations.literal: Beyond this, there must be no further separate solicitation.
translations.idiomatic: No additional exactions of any kind may be imposed.

sentences.zh: 訪聞邊上鎮鋪，於蕃漢戶市易糶糴，衷私有抽稅，今後一切止絕。」

translations.literal: Inquiry heard that frontier garrison markets, in buying and selling grain with Tibetan and Han households, privately impose taxes in the heart; henceforth all of this is to be entirely stopped.'
translations.idiomatic: Reports also show that frontier garrison markets secretly levied taxes on grain trade with Tibetan and Han customers; such charges are henceforth forbidden entirely.

translations.literal: open editorial bracket

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》：周廣順二年九月十八日，敕：「條流禁私鹽曲法如後：一、諸色犯鹽曲，所犯一斤已下至一兩，杖八十，配役；

translations.literal: (Five Dynasties Essentials: Zhou, Guangshun year 2, ninth month, eighteenth day, edict: 'Detailed regulations prohibiting private salt and leaven are as follows: 1. For all sorts of salt and leaven violations, from one jin down to one liang, eighty blows with the staff, plus corvée assignment;'
translations.idiomatic: (Documentary History of the Five Dynasties: On the eighteenth day of the ninth month of Guangshun 2, an edict laid out private salt and leaven prohibitions: First, smuggling one jin down to one liang of salt or leaven merited eighty blows and corvée service;

sentences.zh: 五斤以下一斤以上，徒三年，配役；

translations.literal: Below five jin and above one jin, penal servitude three years, plus corvée assignment;
translations.idiomatic: from one jin up to but not including five jin, three years' penal servitude plus corvée;

sentences.zh: 五斤以上，並決重杖一頓，處死。

translations.literal: Five jin and above, all receive one round of heavy beating, then execution.
translations.idiomatic: five jin or more brought a beating and execution.

sentences.zh: 一、應所犯鹽曲，關津門司、廂巡門保，如有透漏，並行勘斷。

translations.literal: 1. Concerning violated salt and leaven, pass posts, gate clerks, ward patrols, and neighborhood watches—if there is leakage, all are to be investigated and sentenced.
translations.idiomatic: Gatekeepers, ward patrols, and neighborhood watches along transport routes who let contraband through faced the same investigation and punishment.

sentences.zh: 一、刮鹼煎煉私鹽，所犯一斤已下，徒三年，配役；

translations.literal: 1. Scraping alkaline earth to boil private salt: violations of one jin and below, penal servitude three years, plus corvée assignment;
translations.idiomatic: Boiling illicit salt from scraped alkaline earth: one jin or less meant three years' penal servitude plus corvée;

sentences.zh: 一斤以上，並決重杖一頓，處死。

translations.literal: One jin and above, all receive one round of heavy beating, then execution.
translations.idiomatic: more than one jin brought a beating and execution.

sentences.zh: 犯私鹽若捉到堿水，只煎成鹽，秤盤定罪，逐處凡有鹼鹵之地，所在官吏節級所由，常須巡檢，村坊鄰保，遞相覺察，若有所犯處彰露，並行勘斷。

translations.literal: When private salt is violated, if alkaline brine is seized and only boiled into salt, guilt is fixed by the scales; wherever alkaline brine lands exist, local officials, clerks by rank, and runners must constantly patrol and inspect; village wards and neighboring watches must mutually watch; if violations are exposed, all are investigated and sentenced.
translations.idiomatic: If brine was boiled into salt, the finished weight determined the sentence. Officials and patrolmen had to inspect all alkaline lands constantly, with villagers and neighborhood watches reporting one another; any exposed violation brought full prosecution.

sentences.zh: 一、所犯私鹽，捉事、告事人各支賞錢，以系省錢充。

translations.literal: 1. For violated private salt, catchers and accusers each receive reward cash, paid from provincial treasury funds.
translations.idiomatic: Informants and those who made arrests received cash rewards drawn from provincial funds.

sentences.zh: 至死刑者賞錢五十千，不及死刑者三十千。

translations.literal: Those reaching capital punishment receive fifty thousand cash in reward; those not reaching capital punishment, thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Capital cases paid fifty thousand cash; lesser convictions paid thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 一、顆末鹽各有界分，若將本地分鹽侵越疆界，同諸色犯鹽例科斷。

translations.literal: 1. Grain salt and powdered salt each have boundary divisions; if salt from one's own division crosses boundaries, it is sentenced under the same rules as all sorts of salt violations.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and powdered salt each had defined markets; crossing boundaries with local stock was punished like any other salt offense.

sentences.zh: 一、鄉村人戶，所請蠶鹽，只得將歸零躉供食，不得別將博易貨賣，投托與人。

translations.literal: 1. Rural village households, silkworm salt allotted to them, may only take it home for retail household consumption, and may not separately trade it for goods, sell it, or entrust it to others.
translations.idiomatic: Rural households' allotted silkworm salt was for home consumption only—not for barter, sale, or transfer to others.

sentences.zh: 如違，並同諸色犯鹽例科斷。

translations.literal: If violated, all are sentenced under the same rules as all sorts of salt violations.
translations.idiomatic: Violations were punished under the general salt statutes.

sentences.zh: 若是所請蠶鹽，道路津濟須經過州府縣鎮，委三司明行指揮。

translations.literal: If silkworm salt allotted is transported and must pass through state, prefecture, county, and market posts on roads and ferries, this is entrusted to the Three Departments to issue clear directives.
translations.idiomatic: Transport of allotted silkworm salt through state and local checkpoints required explicit orders from the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 一、凡買鹽曲，並須於官場務內買，若衷私投托興販，其買賣人並同諸色犯鹽曲例科斷。

translations.literal: 1. All purchases of salt and leaven must be made within official market offices; if privately entrusting others to trade, buyers and sellers are all sentenced under the same rules as all sorts of salt and leaven violations.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and leaven had to be bought at official depots; private brokerage or resale by either party triggered the standard contraband penalties.

sentences.zh: 一、諸官場官務，如有羨余出剩鹽曲，並許盡底報官。

translations.literal: 1. At all official markets and offices, if there is surplus salt and leaven remaining, all may fully report it to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Official depots with surplus salt or leaven were required to report it in full.

sentences.zh: 如衷私貨賣者，買賣人並同諸色犯鹽曲例科斷。

translations.literal: If secretly sold, buyers and sellers are all sentenced under the same rules as all sorts of salt and leaven violations.
translations.idiomatic: Secret sale by either party brought the standard contraband penalties.

sentences.zh: 若鹽鋪酒店戶及諸色人與場院衷私貨賣者，並同罪科斷。

translations.literal: If salt shops, wine-house households, and persons of all sorts privately sell with depot yards, all receive the same crime and sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Salt shops, taverns, and private dealers who colluded with depot staff faced equal punishment.

sentences.zh: 一、所犯私鹽曲，有同情共犯者，若是骨肉卑幼奴婢同犯，只罪家長主首。

translations.literal: 1. For violated private salt and leaven with sympathetic co-offenders: if kin, juniors, or slaves jointly offend, only the household head is charged.
translations.idiomatic: When family members, minors, or slaves acted together, only the household head was liable.

sentences.zh: 如家長主首不知情，只罪造意者，余減等科斷。

translations.literal: If the household head did not know, only the instigator is charged; the rest receive reduced-grade sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: If the head was unaware, only the ringleader was fully charged while accomplices received reduced sentences.

sentences.zh: 若是他人同犯，並同罪斷。

translations.literal: If others jointly offend, all receive the same crime and sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Unrelated co-offenders shared equal guilt.

sentences.zh: 若與他人同犯，據逐人腳下所犯斤兩，依輕重斷遣。

translations.literal: If jointly offending with others, according to each person's own violated jin and liang underfoot, sentence is dispatched by severity.
translations.idiomatic: Each accomplice was sentenced according to the weight in his possession.

sentences.zh: 一、州城縣鎮郭下人戶，系屋稅合請鹽者，若是州府，並於城內請給，若是外縣鎮郭下人戶，亦許將鹽歸家供食。

translations.literal: 1. Households under prefecture city, county, and market walls liable for house-tax salt allotments: if at the prefecture, all draw allotment within the city; if households outside county and market walls, they are also permitted to take salt home for consumption.
translations.idiomatic: Households owing house-tax salt in prefectural seats drew allotments inside the city; those in outer counties and market towns could take their ration home.

sentences.zh: 仰本縣預取逐戶合請鹽數目，攢定文賬，部領人戶請拔，勒本處官吏及所在場務，同點檢入城。

translations.literal: The county is ordered in advance to take each household's total allotted salt amount, compile written accounts, lead households to draw allotments, and compel local officials and present depot offices jointly to inspect entry into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Counties had to tally each household's salt entitlement in advance, guide distribution, and require local officials and depots to verify salt brought into the city.

sentences.zh: 若縣鎮郭下人戶，城外別有莊田，亦仰本縣預先分擘開坐，勿令一處分給供使。

translations.literal: If households under county and market walls have separate estate fields outside the walls, the county is also ordered in advance to divide and list them separately, and not allow one place to distribute for use.
translations.idiomatic: Households with farms outside the walls had to be listed separately so one depot could not supply them all.

translations.literal: ' Year 3, twelfth month, edict: 'In all prefectures and outside counties and market cities, residents' house-tax salt—henceforth will not be allotted; the salt money will also not be levied.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the twelfth month of year 3, an edict declared that house-tax salt allotments in prefectural and market seats would cease, and salt-money payments would no longer be collected.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年十二月，世宗謂侍臣曰：「朕覽食末鹽州郡，犯私鹽多於顆鹽界分，蓋卑濕之地，易為刮鹼煎造，豈惟違我榷法，兼又汙我好鹽。

translations.literal: Xiande year 1, twelfth month, Shizong said to attendant ministers: 'I observe prefectures eating powdered salt violate private salt more than grain-salt boundaries, because low damp lands easily allow scraping alkaline earth to boil manufacture—not only violating our monopoly law but also polluting our good salt.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Xiande 1, Emperor Shizong told his ministers: 'Powdered-salt regions see more smuggling than grain-salt zones because damp lowlands make illicit boiling from alkaline earth easy—not only breaching our monopoly but tainting quality salt.'

sentences.zh: 況末鹽煎煉，般運費用倍於顆鹽。

translations.literal: Moreover, boiling powdered salt—transport costs are double those of grain salt.
translations.idiomatic: Boiling and shipping powdered salt also costs twice as much as grain salt.

sentences.zh: 今宜分割十餘州，令食顆鹽，不惟輦運省力，兼且少人犯禁。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to divide off more than ten prefectures and make them eat grain salt—not only saving effort in cart transport but also reducing people who violate prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten prefectures should be switched to grain salt—easing transport and cutting violations.

sentences.zh: 」自是曹、宋已西十餘州，皆盡食顆鹽。

translations.literal: ' From this, from Cao and Song westward, more than ten prefectures all entirely ate grain salt.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, a dozen prefectures from Cao and Song westward switched entirely to grain salt.

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》：顯德二年八月二十四日，宣頭節文：「改立鹽法如後：一、贍國軍堂場務、邢洺州鹽務，應有見垛貯鹽貨處，並煎鹽場竈及應是鹼地，並須四面修置墻塹。

translations.literal: (Five Dynasties Essentials: Xiande year 2, eighth month, twenty-fourth day, imperial rescript excerpt: 'Revised salt law established as follows: 1. Shanguo Army hall depots, Xing and Mozhou salt offices—all places where stored salt goods are piled, all boiling salt furnaces, and all alkaline lands must have walls and moats built on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: (Documentary History of the Five Dynasties: On the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month of Xiande 2, a rescript revised salt law: First, Shanguo Army depots and Xing-Mo salt offices—every salt store, boiling furnace, and alkaline tract—required perimeter walls and ditches.

sentences.zh: 如是地裏遙遠，難為修置墻塹，即作壕籬為規隔。

translations.literal: If the land is remote and far, making wall and moat construction difficult, then make trench fences as regulated barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Remote sites unable to support full walls could use trench fences instead.

sentences.zh: 如是人於壕籬內偷盜，夾帶官鹽，兼於壕籬外煎造鹽貨，便仰收捉，及許諸色人陳告。

translations.literal: If persons inside trench fences steal or smuggle official salt, and also boil salt goods outside trench fences, then arrest is ordered, and persons of all sorts may lodge accusations.
translations.idiomatic: Theft inside the fences, smuggling of official salt, or boiling outside them warranted arrest; anyone could report offenders.

sentences.zh: 所犯不計多少斤兩，並決重杖一頓，處死。

translations.literal: Violations, regardless of jin and liang weight, all receive one round of heavy beating, then execution.
translations.idiomatic: Regardless of quantity, offenders received a beating and execution.

sentences.zh: 其經歷地分及門司節級人員，並當量罪勘斷。

translations.literal: Officials of traversed districts and gate clerks by rank must all receive measured-crime investigation and sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Officials along the route and gatekeepers faced proportionate investigation and punishment.

sentences.zh: 所有捉事、告事人賞錢，一兩以上至一斤，賞錢二十千；

translations.literal: All catchers and accusers—reward cash: from one liang up to one jin, twenty thousand cash;
translations.idiomatic: Informants and arresters earned twenty thousand cash for seizures from one liang up to one jin;

sentences.zh: 一斤已上至十斤，賞錢三十千；

translations.literal: from one jin up to ten jin, thirty thousand cash;
translations.idiomatic: one to ten jin paid thirty thousand;

sentences.zh: 一十斤已上，賞錢五十千。

translations.literal: Ten jin and above, fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: ten jin or more paid fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 一、應有不系官中煎鹽處鹼地，並須標識，委本州府差公幹職員與巡檢節級、村保、地主、鄰人，同共巡檢。

translations.literal: 1. Concerning alkaline lands at non-official boiling sites, all must be marked; the prefecture is entrusted to dispatch capable clerks together with patrol officers, village watches, landlords, and neighbors jointly to patrol and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Unmonitored alkaline lands had to be marked; prefectures were to assign officers, patrolmen, village watches, landlords, and neighbors to joint inspection.

sentences.zh: 若諸色人偷刮鹵地，便仰收捉，及許人陳告。

translations.literal: If persons of all sorts secretly scrape brine lands, arrest is ordered, and people may lodge accusations.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone secretly scraping brine lands was to be seized; reports were encouraged.

sentences.zh: 若勘逐不虛，捉事人每獲一人，賞絹一十匹；

translations.literal: If investigation proves true, catchers receive for each person seized ten bolts of silk;
translations.idiomatic: Verified arrests paid the catcher ten bolts of silk per person;

sentences.zh: 獲二人，賞絹二十匹；

translations.literal: two persons seized, twenty bolts;
translations.idiomatic: two persons, twenty bolts;

sentences.zh: 獲三人已上，不計人數，賞絹五十匹。

translations.literal: three persons and above seized, regardless of head count, fifty bolts.
translations.idiomatic: three or more, fifty bolts regardless of total.

sentences.zh: 刮鹼煎鹽人並知情人，所犯不計多少斤兩，並決重杖一頓，處死。

translations.literal: Those who scrape alkaline earth to boil salt and those who know, regardless of jin and liang, all receive one round of heavy beating, then execution.
translations.idiomatic: Scrapers, boilers, and knowing accomplices faced beating and execution regardless of weight.

sentences.zh: 其刮鹼處地分，並刮鹼人住處巡檢、節級、所由、村保等，各徒二年半，令眾一月，依舊勾當。

translations.literal: At the district of scraping, and at residence districts of scrapers—patrol officers, clerks by rank, runners, village watches, and the like—each penal servitude two and a half years, public display one month, then resume duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: Patrolmen, clerks, runners, and village watches in the affected districts received two and a half years' penal servitude, one month on public display, then returned to duty.

sentences.zh: 刮堿處地主，不切檢校，徒二年，令眾一月。

translations.literal: Landlords at scraping sites who do not strictly inspect receive penal servitude two years, public display one month.
translations.idiomatic: Negligent landlords at scraping sites received two years' penal servitude and one month on display.

sentences.zh: 一、顆鹽地分界內，有人刮鹼煎煉鹽貨，所犯並依前法。

translations.literal: 1. Within grain-salt boundary divisions, if anyone scrapes alkaline earth to boil salt goods, violations all follow the preceding law.
translations.idiomatic: Inside grain-salt boundaries, illicit boiling from alkaline earth was punished under the same rules.

sentences.zh: 一、今緣改價賣鹽，慮有別界分鹽貨遞相侵犯，及將鹽入城，諸色犯鹽人，令下三司，依下項條流科斷；

translations.literal: 1. Now because salt is sold at revised prices, fearing salt goods from other boundaries may mutually invade, and bringing salt into cities—all sorts of salt violators—the Three Departments are ordered to sentence under the following detailed regulations;
translations.idiomatic: With salt prices revised, cross-boundary smuggling and bringing salt into cities were referred to the Three Departments under the following articles;

sentences.zh: 其犯鹽人隨行物色，給與本家，其鹽沒納入官。

translations.literal: The violator's accompanying goods are given to his household; the salt is confiscated to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Personal goods went to the offender's family; salt was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 所經歷地分節級人員，並行勘斷。

translations.literal: Officials by rank in traversed districts all receive investigation and sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Officials along the route were also prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 一兩至一斤，決臀杖十五，令眾半月，捉事、告事人賞錢五千；

translations.literal: One liang to one jin: fifteen blows of hip staff, public display half a month, catchers and accusers five thousand cash reward;
translations.idiomatic: One liang to one jin: fifteen hip-staff blows, two weeks on display, five thousand cash to informants;

sentences.zh: 一斤已上至一十斤，徒一年半，令眾一月，捉事、告事人賞錢七千；

translations.literal: one jin up to ten jin: penal servitude one and a half years, public display one month, seven thousand cash reward;
translations.idiomatic: one to ten jin: eighteen months' penal servitude, one month on display, seven thousand cash;

sentences.zh: 十斤已上，不計多少，徒二年，配發運務役一年，捉事、告事人賞錢十千。

translations.literal: Ten jin and above, regardless of amount: penal servitude two years, assigned one year corvée at transport offices, ten thousand cash reward.
translations.idiomatic: Ten jin or more: two years' penal servitude, one year transport corvée, ten thousand cash to informants.

sentences.zh: 一、諸州府人戶所請蠶鹽，不得於鄉村衷私貨賣，及信團頭、腳戶、縣司、請鹽節級、所由等克折糶賣，如有犯者，依諸色犯鹽例科斷。

translations.literal: 1. Silkworm salt allotted to prefecture households must not be secretly sold in villages, nor sold at reduced price by trust-group heads, porters, county clerks, salt-allotment officers, runners, and the like; violators are sentenced under all sorts of salt violation rules.
translations.idiomatic: Allotted silkworm salt could not be secretly sold in villages or resold at a markup by group heads, porters, county clerks, or salt clerks; violations brought standard salt penalties.

sentences.zh: 一、如有人於河東界將鹽過來，及自家界內有人往彼興販鹽貨，所犯者並處斬。

translations.literal: 1. If anyone brings salt across from Hedong boundary, or within one's own boundary anyone goes there to trade salt goods, all violators are executed by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Smuggling salt from Hedong or trading salt across that boundary merited decapitation.

sentences.zh: 其犯鹽人隨行驢畜資財，並與捉事人充賞。

translations.literal: The violator's accompanying donkeys, livestock, and property all go to catchers as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Donkeys, livestock, and goods went to the arresting party as reward.

translations.idiomatic: At Qingzhou's green-white monopoly office, existing anti-evasion rules split seized donkeys and goods half to arresters and half with the salt to the state.

translations.literal: It is intended also to follow the old rules: from one dou up to three dou, seventy blows; from three dou up to five dou, penal servitude one year; five dou and above, execution.
translations.idiomatic: Evaders of one to three dou received seventy blows; three to five dou, one year's penal servitude; five dou or more, death—as before.

sentences.zh: 安邑、解縣兩池榷鹽院，河府節度使兼判之時申到畫一事件條流等，準敕牒，兩池所出鹽，舊日苦無文榜，如擅將一斤一兩，準元敕條，並處極法。

translations.literal: Anyi and Jie county two pool monopoly salt offices—when the Hedong circuit military commissioner concurrently judged, submitted unified case regulations, etc., per edict documents: salt produced by the two pools, in old days bitterly lacked posted regulations; if one jin or one liang is taken without authorization, under original edict articles, all receive the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hedong military commissioner oversaw the Anyi and Jie salt pools, unified rules under imperial orders held that even one jin or liang taken without authorization merited the extreme penalty—though old posted regulations had been lacking.

sentences.zh: 其犯鹽人應有錢物，並與捉事人充賞者。

translations.literal: The violator's due cash and goods all go to catchers as reward.
translations.idiomatic: The offender's cash and goods went to arresters as reward.

sentences.zh: 切以兩池禁棘峻阻，不通人行，四面各置場門弓射，分擘鹽池地分居住，並在棘圍裏面，更不別有差遣，只令巡護鹽池。

translations.literal: Strictly, the two pools' thorn barriers are steep and blocked, impassable to persons; on four sides each place depot gates and archers; salt pool districts are divided for residence—all inside thorn enclosures, with no further separate assignments, only ordered to patrol and guard the salt pools.
translations.idiomatic: The two pools were ringed by steep thorn barriers impassable to outsiders, with gated posts and archers on all sides; residents inside the enclosure had no other duty but guarding the pools.

sentences.zh: 如此後有人偷盜官鹽一斤一兩出池，其犯鹽人並準元敕條流處分，應有隨行錢物並納入官，其捉事人依下項定支優給。

translations.literal: If thereafter anyone steals one jin or one liang of official salt out of the pools, all salt violators are disposed of under original edict regulations; accompanying cash and goods all enter the government; catchers receive fixed generous rewards below.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone stealing even one jin or liang from the pools faced original penalties; goods were forfeited to the state while arresters received the stipulated generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 若是巡檢、弓射、池場門子，自不專切巡察，致有透漏到棘圍外，被別人捉獲，及有糾告，兼同行反告，官中更不坐罪，陳告人亦依捉事人支賞。

translations.literal: If patrol officers, archers, and pool gate keepers themselves do not devotedly patrol and inspect, causing leakage outside the thorn enclosure to be seized by others, with accusations and mutual counter-accusations among peers—the government no longer imposes crime on them; accusers also receive rewards like catchers.
translations.idiomatic: If guards failed to patrol and outsiders made the arrest, peers who reported one another faced no official penalty; accusers received catcher-level rewards.

sentences.zh: 應有知情偷盜官鹽之人，亦依犯鹽人一例處斷。

translations.literal: All who knowingly steal official salt are also disposed of in the same manner as salt violators.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing accomplices in salt theft were punished like the principal offenders.

sentences.zh: 其不知情關連人，臨時酌情定罪。

translations.literal: Those unknowingly connected are sentenced at the time according to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Unwitting associates were sentenced case by case.

sentences.zh: 所有透漏地分弓射及池場門子，如是透漏出鹽一十斤已下，徒一年半。

translations.literal: All archers and pool gate keepers in leaky districts—if leakage is ten jin and below, penal servitude one and a half years.
translations.idiomatic: Archers and gatekeepers through whose posts salt leaked—when the leak was ten jin or less—received one and a half years' penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 一十斤已上至二十斤，支賞錢一十千；

translations.literal: from ten jin up to twenty jin, ten thousand cash reward;
translations.idiomatic: From ten to twenty jin, informants received ten thousand cash;

sentences.zh: 二十斤已上至五十斤，支賞錢二十千；

translations.literal: from twenty jin up to fifty jin, twenty thousand cash reward;
translations.idiomatic: twenty to fifty jin paid twenty thousand cash;

sentences.zh: 五十斤已上至一百斤，支賞錢三十千；

translations.literal: from fifty jin up to one hundred jin, thirty thousand cash reward;
translations.idiomatic: fifty to one hundred jin paid thirty thousand cash;

sentences.zh: 一百斤已上，支賞錢五十千。

translations.literal: One hundred jin and above, fifty thousand cash reward.
translations.idiomatic: one hundred jin or more paid fifty thousand cash.

translations.literal: For the preceding fixed salt-law regulations on seized violators, those falling under prefecture jurisdiction—once caught, the home prefecture is entrusted to examine regulations, sentence, report upward, and separately notify the provincial office.

translations.literal: Those salt violators caught by provincial offices—if involving capital punishment—investigate circumstances and crimes and report upward, awaiting provincial office directives.

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

translations.literal: Year 3, tenth month, edict: 'North of the Zhang River, within prefecture jurisdictions, originally official markets sold salt; henceforth except within city walls and country markets, old prohibitions remain; in villages salt goods free trade is all permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 3, an edict declared that north of the Zhang River, outside city walls and country markets where the old monopoly still applied, villages might freely trade salt.

sentences.zh: 逐處有鹼鹵之地，一任人戶煎煉，興販則不得逾越漳河，入不通商地界。」

translations.literal: Wherever alkaline brine lands exist, households are entirely free to boil; in trading they must not cross the Zhang River into non-free-trade territory.'
translations.idiomatic: Households might boil salt wherever alkaline brine existed, but traders could not cross the Zhang River into restricted zones.'

translations.literal: Zhou, Xiande year 2, first month, Shizong said to attendant ministers: 'Goods in transport—formerly all were granted dou allowance for loss; since Jin and Han, none has been granted replacement.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhou Xiande 2, Shizong told his ministers: 'Transported grain once included a loss allowance per dou, but since Later Jin and Han that allowance has gone unpaid.

sentences.zh: 倉廩所納新物，尚除省耗，況水路所般，豈無損折？

translations.literal: Even new goods received into granaries still deduct provincial loss allowance—how much more goods transported by water route, can there be no damage and break?
translations.idiomatic: Granaries even deduct standard storage loss from fresh deliveries—how can water transport suffer no spoilage?

sentences.zh: 起今後每石宜與耗一斗。」

translations.literal: From now on on each shi it is fitting to grant one dou loss allowance.'
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth each shi shall carry a one-dou transport allowance.'

sentences.zh: 唐天成三年七月，詔曰：「應三京、鄴都、諸道州府鄉村人戶，自今年七月後，於是秋田苗上，每畝納曲錢五文足陌，一任百姓自造私曲，醞酒供家，其錢隨夏秋征納。

translations.literal: Tang, Tiancheng year 3, seventh month, edict: 'All village households in the three capitals, Yedu, and circuit prefectures—from this seventh month onward, on autumn field seedlings, each mu pays five cash leaven money at full count; commoners are entirely free to make private leaven and brew wine for household use; the money is levied with summer and autumn collections.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tiancheng 3 (928), an edict required rural households in the capitals, Yedu, and all circuits to pay five cash leaven tax per mu on autumn crops, while permitting private brewing for home use; payment fell due with summer and autumn tax.

sentences.zh: 其京都及諸道州府縣鎮坊界內，應逐年買官曲酒戶，便許自造曲，醞酒貨賣。

translations.literal: Within the capital and circuit prefecture, county, and market ward boundaries—yearly official-leaven wine-shop households are permitted to make leaven themselves and brew wine for sale.
translations.idiomatic: In urban wards, licensed wine-shop households could brew their own leaven and sell wine.

sentences.zh: 仍取天成二年正月至年終一年逐戶計算都買曲錢數內，十分只納二分，以充榷酒錢，便從今年七月後，管數征納。

translations.literal: Still taking from Tiancheng year 2, first month to year end, one year's per-household total official-leaven purchase money—of ten parts pay only two parts as monopoly wine money; from this seventh month collect on that basis.
translations.idiomatic: They would pay only two-tenths of their Tiancheng 2 official-leaven purchases as the wine monopoly fee, collected from the seventh month onward.

sentences.zh: 榷酒戶外，其餘諸色人亦許私造酒曲供家，即不得衷私賣酒，如有故違，便即糾察，勒依中等酒戶納榷。

translations.literal: Outside monopoly wine households, other persons of all sorts are also permitted to make wine and leaven privately for household use, but must not secretly sell wine; if deliberately violated, immediately investigate, and compel payment of monopoly tax as a medium-grade wine household.
translations.idiomatic: Others might brew for home use but not sell secretly; violators were assessed as medium-grade wine shops.

sentences.zh: 其坊村一任沽賣，不在納榷之限。

translations.literal: In wards and villages, free sale is entirely permitted, not within monopoly-payment limits.
translations.idiomatic: Wards and villages remained free to sell without monopoly limits.

sentences.zh: 」時孔循以曲法殺一家於洛陽，或獻此議，以為愛其人，便於國，故行之。

translations.literal: ' At the time Kong Xun by leaven law killed one household in Luoyang; someone offered this proposal, holding that loving the people benefits the state, and so it was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xun had executed a family in Luoyang under the old leaven law; supporters argued this reform would spare the people and serve the state, and it was adopted.

sentences.zh: 長興元年二月，赦書節文：「諸道州府人戶，每秋苗一畝上，元征曲錢五文，今後特放二文，只征三文。

translations.literal: Changxing year 1, second month, amnesty excerpt: 'Households in circuit prefectures, on each mu of autumn seedlings, originally levied five cash leaven money—henceforth specially remit two cash, levy only three.
translations.idiomatic: The Changxing 1 (930) amnesty cut the autumn leaven levy from five to three cash per mu.

sentences.zh: 」二年，詔曰：「酒醴所重，曲糵是須，緣賣價太高，禁條頗峻，士庶因斯而抵犯，刑名由是以滋彰。

translations.literal: ' Year 2, edict: 'Wine is valued; leaven and malt are essential—because sale prices were too high and prohibitions quite severe, gentry and commoners therefore offended, and criminal names thereby grew conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, an edict observed that steep prices and harsh bans had driven citizens into crime and swollen the dockets.

sentences.zh: 爰行改革之文，庶息煩苛之政，各隨苗畝，量定稅錢。

translations.literal: Therefore carry out reform documents, hoping to rest from troublesome harsh governance; each follows seedling mu, measuring and fixing tax money.
translations.idiomatic: Reforms were issued to end excessive harshness, with tax fixed per cultivated mu.

sentences.zh: 訪聞數年已來，雖犯法者稀，而傷民則甚。

translations.literal: Inquiry heard that in several years since, though violators are few, harm to the people is great.
translations.idiomatic: Reports showed that though violations had grown rare, the burden on the people remained severe.

sentences.zh: 蓋以亂離日久，貧下戶多，才遇升平，便勤稼穡，各務耕田鑿井，孰能枕曲藉糟，既隨例以均攤，遂抱虛而輸納，漸成雕敝，深可憫傷。

translations.literal: For disorder and separation had lasted long, poor households were many; they had just met peace and at once labored in farming, each striving to plow fields and sink wells—who could rest on leaven and lie on dregs? Yet because levies were spread by rule, they paid in while holding nothing, gradually becoming worn down—a matter deeply pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: After years of chaos, poor households were numerous; when peace finally came they threw themselves into farming and digging wells rather than drinking—yet they still paid leaven taxes by formula while having nothing to sell, growing ever poorer, a plight that truly merited compassion.

sentences.zh: 況欲致豐財，必除時病，有利之事，方切施行，無名之求，尤宜廢罷，但得日新之理，何辭夕改之嫌。

translations.literal: Moreover, to bring abundant wealth, present ills must be removed; what is beneficial is then urgently applied, nameless demands are especially fit to abolish—if only the principle of daily renewal is obtained, why shrink from the suspicion of evening change?
translations.idiomatic: To enrich the treasury, present abuses had to go: useful measures should be enacted at once and pointless exactions abolished; where daily improvement was possible, the court need not fear charges of changing policy overnight.

sentences.zh: 應在京諸道苗畝上所征曲錢等，便從今年夏並放。

translations.literal: The leaven money and the like levied on field seedlings in the capital and all circuits are from this year's summer all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Leaven taxes on autumn seedlings in the capital and every circuit were remitted starting that summer.

sentences.zh: 其曲官中自造，委逐州減舊價一半，於在城撲斷貨賣。

translations.literal: Leaven is made by the government itself; each prefecture is commissioned to cut the old price in half and sell by monopoly auction within the city.
translations.idiomatic: The state would brew leaven itself, ordering each prefecture to halve the old price and sell it exclusively within urban markets.

sentences.zh: 除在城居人不得私造外，鄉村人戶或要供家，一任私造。

translations.literal: Except that city dwellers may not make it privately, rural households who need it for household supply may freely make it themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Urban residents could not brew privately, but rural families needing leaven for home use were free to make their own.

sentences.zh: 」敕下之日，人甚悅之。

translations.literal: ' On the day the edict descended, the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was promulgated, the populace rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 周顯德四年七月，詔曰：「諸道州府曲務，今後一依往例，官中禁法賣曲，逐處先置都務，候敕到日，並仰停罷。

translations.literal: Zhou, seventh month of Xiande year 4, edict: 'Leaven offices in circuit prefectures and districts—hereafter entirely follow past practice: the government sells leaven under prohibition law; everywhere the previously established chief offices, when the edict arrives, are all ordered to cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhou Xiande 4 (957), an edict declared that circuit leaven monopolies would revert to the old state monopoly: local chief offices set up earlier were to shut down when the order arrived.

sentences.zh: 據見在曲數，準備貨買，兼據年計合，使曲數依時蹋造，候人戶將到價錢，據數計曲，不得賒賣抑配與人。」

translations.literal: According to existing leaven quantities, prepare goods for trade; also according to the yearly total, have leaven produced on schedule; when households bring ready payment, calculate leaven by quantity—credit sale and forced allotment to people are not permitted.'
translations.idiomatic: Stock on hand was to be readied for sale, annual requirements scheduled for timely production, and leaven issued only after full cash payment in measured amounts—no credit sales or forced allocations.
